name: @johnhenry/temporals-viaframe
description: Calendar and duration panes for viaframe, from @johnhenry/temporals: working hours (open now? next opening), business time between two moments, adding business days over holidays, durations in words, relative time and RRULE occurrences. Offline: no network, no server.

panes.title: Working hours
panes.description: Is a schedule open at a moment, and if not, when does it open next? Working windows in a time zone, a weekend and holidays (the US federal list, Easter-based days, fixed dates) give `open`, `closesAt`, `nextOpen` and the wait in milliseconds and in words.

Working windows as [open, close] wall-clock times, read in `zone`. A window that ends before it starts crosses midnight (["22:00", "06:00"]).

panes.title: Business time between
panes.description: The working time between two moments under a schedule (windows, a weekend, holidays), in milliseconds, hours and words, and how many working days the stretch touches. Friday 15:00 to Monday 11:00 on a 09:00 to 17:00 week is 4 hours.

panes.description: Move a date by a number of working days (negative goes back), skipping the weekend and holidays, and list the days off it skipped. Three working days from 23 December 2026 with the US federal holidays is Tuesday 29 December.

panes.title: Duration in words
panes.description: A duration as words. Takes milliseconds, an ISO 8601 duration (PT1H30M, P2W3D) or shorthand (1h 30m), and gives "1 day, 2 hours" (or "1d 2h" with `short`), its ISO form, and its milliseconds when it has a fixed length. `maxUnits` keeps the largest units; `locale` localizes where Intl.DurationFormat exists.

control.help: Milliseconds (93784000), an ISO 8601 duration (PT1H30M, P2W) or shorthand (1h 30m, 2d 12h).
Keep only this many of the largest units; 0 keeps every one.
1h 30m instead of 1 hour, 30 minutes.
The smallest unit shown.
A locale (fr, de-CH) for localized words where the runtime has Intl.DurationFormat; empty is English.

panes.title: Relative time
panes.description: One time said relative to another, with Intl.RelativeTimeFormat ("in 2 days", "tomorrow", "3 hours ago") in a locale. Days are calendar days in `zone`, so the 26 hours from 23:00 on one day to 01:00 two days later are "in 2 days" (less than a day is said in hours). Also the time between, in words.

control.help: The time it is said from: ISO with an offset or Z, with a [zone], a wall-clock time read in `zone`, or "now".
Calendar days (tomorrow, in 2 days) are counted in this zone.
auto says tomorrow and yesterday; always says in 1 day.

panes.title: Next occurrences (RRULE)
panes.description: The times of an RFC 5545 recurrence rule (FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE, FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=2TU, COUNT, UNTIL, INTERVAL, …) from a start time in a zone, keeping the wall clock across daylight saving changes. Gives each time with its zone and in UTC, optionally only those after a moment.

control.help: An RFC 5545 RRULE (FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=2TU, FREQ=DAILY;INTERVAL=3, …), with or without RRULE:.
The first time (DTSTART): a wall-clock time read in `zone`, or an ISO time with an offset, Z or [zone].
The zone the rule repeats in: the wall-clock time stays put across daylight saving changes.
How many times to list (1 to 500).
List only the times at or after this one; empty lists from the start.
